projects.goal: Build a registration and credential-verification service that stores password hashes and resolves duplicate identities safely.
deliverables: A register/verify service with no plaintext credential storage

scope: Require email, username and password; normalize email by trimming and lowercasing under an explicitly documented academy policy; reserve a unique normalized username.

projects.goal: Build a complete authorization-code round trip with a local mock provider, browser-bound state and PKCE before using real provider accounts.
deliverables: A browser login start/callback flow and a fake authorization server

projects.title: Google OIDC, GitHub Identity and Account Linking
projects.goal: Connect a tiny account application to both Google and GitHub and map verified provider identities to local members without email-based takeover.
deliverables: Two live provider adapters plus deterministic synthetic tests
A provider setup worksheet, identity schema and explicit link flow
scope: Register test applications with both providers during preparation, configure exact callback URIs and test users, and keep client secrets outside source control. Teacher supplies a tested fallback cohort account when setup is unavailable.
Google uses OpenID Connect: verify the ID-token signature with jose and discovery JWKS, permitted algorithms, issuer, audience, expiry and login-attempt nonce; key identity by issuer+sub.

GitHub uses OAuth access token to retrieve the authenticated user; key by provider+numeric id, not mutable login name. Read /user/emails only with needed scope and select a verified email if one is required.

Store a unique provider+subject mapping to a local member. First login creates a member after username onboarding; repeat login reuses it; no verified email means require local onboarding rather than invent one.

Never auto-link by matching email. Linking requires an existing authenticated member, recent reauthentication and a separately bound link intent; the provider identity cannot already belong to another member.

Issue the same P10 forum session after successful identity resolution. Access and refresh tokens are not rendered or placed in browser storage; discard provider tokens after profile use unless a documented server-side use requires retention.

scope: Accept decoded JPEG, PNG and GIF only, regardless of extension or declared MIME. Decode with Sharp; metadata inspection alone is not proof a compressed file is valid.
Academy limits: width and height each 1–8192, at most 25,000,000 pixels per frame, at most 100 GIF frames and 100,000,000 total decoded pixels. Reject oversized or corrupt images with 422.

A post may have text and one image or text only. Publish the post only after validation and finalized file placement; database failure triggers file cleanup, and a reconciliation tool identifies crash leftovers.

projects.title: Session Attack and Browser Defense Workbench
projects.goal: Attack a disposable mini board with forged tokens, fixation, CSRF and content injection, then prove that server-side defenses hold under concurrent requests.
deliverables: A threat model mapped to automated attack fixtures
A server-session hardening and safe-header regression report
scope: Test session fixation, forged token, copied expired token, two simultaneous logins, logout replay and revoked-session reuse against SQLite-backed state.
Rotate identifiers after authentication and privilege changes, store only token digests, enforce absolute and idle expiry; academy idle timeout is 30 minutes and absolute timeout 8 hours.

requirements.text: Hold new posts pending until authorized approval; publish or reject through auditable transitions; authors see their own pending status and moderators cannot self-approve.
requirements.verify: Pending content is public only after approved transition.

requirements.text: Moderators can delete existing posts and report posts to administrators with a stored reason.
requirements.verify: Delete and report routes enforce moderator role.

requirements.text: Users can request moderator status; admin can approve/reject the request and promote or demote users to/from moderator.
requirements.verify: Role request and audited decision persist.

requirements.text: Admins receive reports, respond to them and resolve them; reporter can read the persisted response.
requirements.verify: Report→admin inbox→response→resolution demonstrated.

requirements.text: Admins can delete both posts and comments. Deleted content is excluded from public views.
requirements.verify: Direct comment deletion by admin succeeds; ordinary member denied.

requirements.text: Admins can create and delete categories; an attached category deletion returns 409 under the prepared retention policy.
requirements.verify: Unused category deleted; attached category remains intact.

requirements.text: Bootstrap admin through the operator procedure; public registration cannot assign privileged roles; protect the final admin.
requirements.verify: Role spoof and final-admin race fail safely.

requirements.text: Read current roles on every action, apply demotion immediately, guard all detail/feed/filter/count routes and installed image assets against pending/deleted leakage.
requirements.verify: Old demoted cookie and guessed restricted IDs fail.

requirements.text: Enforce expected-state/version transitions atomically with actor/reason/time audit; conflicting reviews return 409; retain F01 and installed-feature checks.
requirements.verify: Simultaneous approve/reject has one winner and one conflict.

requirements.text: Notify post owners when other members comment or change a post reaction to like/dislike; do not notify self-actions or unchanged repeated reactions.
requirements.verify: One correct recipient notification per meaningful change.

requirements.text: Persist notification intent with the domain change, deliver idempotently and authorize recipient-only reads/read-marking.
requirements.verify: Rollback creates no event; dispatcher replay creates no duplicate.

requirements.text: Provide durable offline notification inbox with read/unread state; normal refresh is the required transport and optional real-time delivery must have separate completed prep.
requirements.verify: Offline recipient sees committed notifications on next visit.
requirements.origin: Academy delivery contract; source does not mandate a push protocol

requirements.text: Activity page shows the logged-in user’s authored posts and where they currently liked/disliked posts or comments.
requirements.verify: Cleared/switched reactions move to correct current sections.

requirements.text: Activity page shows where and what the user commented, including comment text plus parent post context and a permitted link or neutral tombstone.
requirements.verify: Comment fixture includes both content and parent context.

requirements.text: Provide owner-only edit/remove sections for both posts and comments, with server ownership checks and CSRF protection.
requirements.verify: Nonowner spoof fails; owner edits/removes both content types.

requirements.text: Reject stale edits with 409 using expected versions; soft deletion applies the prepared child, reaction, asset and notification visibility policy.
requirements.verify: Two editors cannot silently overwrite; deleted parents do not leak.

requirements.text: If moderation is installed, editing published content requeues it for review and withdraws public/asset visibility until approved; privileged overrides follow its matrix.
requirements.verify: Moderated edit becomes pending; no public leak.

requirements.text: Use session-derived activity ownership, stable bounded pagination, correct SQL and justified indexes; retain all installed-feature tests.
requirements.verify: Actor spoof fails; exact rows unchanged by index optimization.

requirements.text: Optional genuine live-database encryption and key recovery; ordinary SQLite plus PRAGMA key is insufficient.
requirements.verify: Right-key/incorrect-key/ordinary-reader, export parity, rotation and encrypted restore checks.
